description:
You are an expert in TRNSYS energy system simulation. Please build a TRNSYS-based water-to-water heat pump domestic hot water system simulation model to study the performance of a single-stage water-to-water heat pump coupled with a stratified hot water storage tank for domestic hot water supply over a one-week period.

Simulation runs from hour 0 to hour 168 (7 days, corresponding to one week), with a time step of 0.125 hours (7.5 minutes).

The system consists of a single-stage water-to-water heat pump (using normalized performance data files), a stratified hot water storage tank with fixed inlets and uniform losses (3 nodes), two single-speed pumps (one on the tank loop and one on the ground-source loop), a differential controller with hysteresis for heat pump on/off control, a time-dependent forcing function providing a constant mains water temperature, and a time-dependent forcing function defining a daily domestic hot water draw schedule. No weather file is required for this simulation.

Water-to-water heat pump parameters (normalized data file approach):
- Source fluid specific heat: 4.19 kJ/(kg·K)
- Load fluid specific heat: 4.19 kJ/(kg·K)
- Source fluid density: 1000 kg/m³
- Load fluid density: 1000 kg/m³
- Number of source temperatures for cooling data: 6
- Number of load temperatures for cooling data: 4
- Number of source temperatures for heating data: 5
- Number of load temperatures for heating data: 4
- Number of source flowrates: 3
- Number of load flowrates: 3
- Rated cooling capacity per heat pump: 30000 kJ/h (approximately 8.33 kW)
- Rated cooling power per heat pump: 6000 kJ/h (approximately 1.67 kW)
- Rated heating capacity per heat pump: 30000 kJ/h (approximately 8.33 kW)
- Rated heating power per heat pump: 6000 kJ/h (approximately 1.67 kW)
- Rated source flowrate per heat pump: 0.4 L/s
- Rated load flowrate per heat pump: 0.4 L/s
- Number of identical heat pumps: 1
- Cooling performance data file: "d:\TRNSYS18_03\Tess Models\SampleCatalogData\Water-to-WaterHeatPump\Normalized\WWHP_Cooling-Normalized.dat"
- Heating performance data file: "d:\TRNSYS18_03\Tess Models\SampleCatalogData\Water-to-WaterHeatPump\Normalized\WWHP_Heating-Normalized.dat"

Stratified hot water storage tank parameters (3-node, fixed inlets, uniform losses):
- Tank volume: 0.3 m³
- Fluid specific heat: 4.19 kJ/(kg·K)
- Fluid density: 1000 kg/m³
- Tank loss coefficient: 3 kJ/(h·m²·K)
- Number of tank nodes: 3
- Height of each node: 0.5 m (total tank height: 1.5 m)
- Auxiliary heater mode: master-slave
- Auxiliary heater element 1: located in node 1, thermostat in node 1, set point 55°C, deadband 5°C, maximum heating rate 0 kJ/h (disabled)
- Auxiliary heater element 2: located in node 1, thermostat in node 1, set point 55°C, deadband 5°C, maximum heating rate 0 kJ/h (disabled)
- Boiling point: 100°C
- Initial temperature of all 3 nodes: 20°C


Tank-side single-speed pump parameters:
- Maximum flow rate: 1440 kg/h
- Fluid specific heat: 4.19 kJ/(kg·K)
- Maximum power: 1342.281877 kJ/h (approximately 0.37 kW)
- Conversion coefficient (fraction of pump power converted to fluid thermal energy): 0

Ground-source-side single-speed pump parameters:
- Maximum flow rate: 1440 kg/h
- Fluid specific heat: 4.19 kJ/(kg·K)
- Maximum power: 1342.281877 kJ/h (approximately 0.37 kW)
- Conversion coefficient (fraction of pump power converted to fluid thermal energy): 0

Differential controller with hysteresis (successive substitution method):
- Upper input temperature (Th): 55°C (fixed reference set point)
- Lower input temperature (Tl): connected to the average tank temperature
- Monitoring temperature (Tin): connected to the tank top temperature (temperature to load)
- Upper dead band: 10°C
- Lower dead band: 0°C
- High limit cut-out: 100°C
- Number of allowed oscillations: 5
The controller turns on the heat pump and both pumps when the average tank temperature drops below 45°C (55 - 10), and turns them off when the average tank temperature reaches 55°C.

Mains water temperature:
- Constant at 10°C throughout the simulation period (provided by a time-dependent temperature forcing function).

Domestic hot water draw schedule (repeating daily pattern, provided by a time-dependent water draw forcing function):
- 0:00–7:00: 0 kg/h (no draw)
- 7:00–9:00: 50 kg/h (morning draw)
- 9:00–12:00: 0 kg/h (no draw)
- 12:00–13:00: 100 kg/h (midday peak draw)
- 13:00–17:00: 0 kg/h (no draw)
- 17:00–21:00: 50 kg/h (evening draw)
- 21:00–24:00: 0 kg/h (no draw)

System connections:
- The heat pump operates in heating mode only (cooling control signal is fixed at 0, heating control signal is driven by the differential controller).
- The heat pump load side receives water from the tank bottom (via the tank-side pump) and returns heated water to the tank hot-side inlet.
- The heat pump source side receives water from the ground-source pump, which draws water at the constant mains temperature of 10°C (simulating a ground-source water supply).
- Domestic hot water is drawn from the tank top (load side), and cold mains water at 10°C enters the tank bottom to replace the drawn water.
- Both pumps are controlled by the same differential controller output signal.

Output requirements:
- Plot temperature curves including: mains water temperature, average tank temperature, heat pump source-side outlet temperature, heat pump load-side outlet temperature, tank top temperature (to load), and tank bottom temperature (to heat source) on the left axis (range: -20 to 70°C)
- Plot the differential controller output control signal on the right axis (range: 0 to 2)
- Generate 1 plot for the entire simulation period (7 days)
